# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Respondents → the public account each story is based on

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say keeping the schedule on track and getting subs on site matters more than the log, so one group is right, and 'Schedule slipping when subs don't show' is the plain way a super would put it.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line; both are straight answers about what pushes the daily log down the list.

founder.order_why: Name, market, context, problem, then interviews runs the way I'd explain Fresco, but the recency screen (4) sits between two identical context screens (3 and 5), so the context step reads as if it starts over.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same kicker and the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.')
founder.missing: Nothing asked who pays: the general contractor buys per site, not the superintendent. Nothing asked whether the super writes the log themselves or hands it to an assistant super or PM. Nothing asked about the stakes behind the log (liability and owner disputes over delays), which is why accuracy matters and not just time.

PRIMARY.order_why: It goes from whether I'm on Procore, to whether and how often the log ate my hours, to what I'd want easier, to how the photo upload went last time, which follows how my evening actually runs, though screens 1 and 2 both say '1 of 4'.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the log actually took me on a typical day, what else goes into it besides photos (manpower, weather, deliveries, notes from the walks), and whether I've had to pull old logs for a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title with its deciding number 'Frequency: 4 answered', and the Frequency card beside it gives the '5 needed' bar.
screens.why_b2: The Prevalence line '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar' reads at once, but three cards count only 4 while the page says 7 answered, and nothing says where the other three went, so I had to look twice.
screens.why_b3: The Importance and Current solution lines are word for word the beliefs I checked, and Prevalence and Frequency are my own lines from the study.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' hints that I need more answers, but nothing tells me to get them, how many more to get, or what Prevalence holding only at the bar means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: My own pitch ('lose hours of every working day') sits under the verdict as if it were a finding, even though Frequency, the card that would back it, could not be called on 4 answers.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 7 superintendents weren't counted on Frequency, Importance and Current solution (4 counted, 5 needed). Here is why, and get at least one more superintendent to answer. Prevalence held, but only just: 6 of 7, exactly at the bar.

screens.why_b1: "Holding up" sits right beside "6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar", so I see the verdict and the number that decides it together.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows who said yes (6 for, 1 against) out of 7, with the marker at 6 and "at least 8 in 10" turned into 6 of 7, so it reads on first look.
screens.why_b3: I recognise it, but I believed nearly every super keeps a daily log; "spent hours typing it up" adds a time claim that is closer to my pitch than to the prevalence belief.
screens.why_b4: The So line only points me to the next two cards and says nothing about what landing exactly on the bar means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, "a small group: a lean, not a call" says the n is small, and "common among these 7" keeps the claim to the people who answered.
screens.instead: Holding up, just: 6 of 7 superintendents spent hours on the log this week, exactly at your bar, so one more no would flip it; treat it as a lean and see Frequency and Importance before leaning on it.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', so I know why there's no verdict.
screens.why_b2: The bars count picks (8) but the bar is '3 of 4' people, and the strip shows 'for 2, against 6' as if it were people, so I had to work out that only 4 people answered and 2 of them picked the log.
screens.why_b3: Importance and the belief line are word for word what I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say the lean is against me (2 of 4, with schedule and subs on top) or that one more counted super would settle it.
screens.why_b5: n is visible and the small group is named, but a strip reading 'against 6' when only 2 people counted against me overstates the opposition, and 'a lean' never says which way.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of the 4 supers counted put the daily log in their two (3 of 4 needed); schedule and subs took the most picks; one more counted answer decides it.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Too few to call' sits right above the number that decides it, '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: The line is named Importance and the belief is word for word the one I checked: the daily log as one of the two of five they'd most like made easier.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more answer, but the screen never says that outright, and it doesn't say what two supers putting schedule and subs above the log means for Fresco's pitch.
screens.why_b5: The counts stay visible ('2 against · 2 asked their why here', group of 2) and the low n is said in the status line, so no claim goes beyond the two people quoted.
screens.why_b6: I didn't type that the competing pain is subs no-showing and the schedule slipping, or that one super already finishes the log on a tablet before leaving the gate; both sharpen where Fresco's texting-the-crew piece might matter more than the log.
screens.instead: Too few to call: one more answer settles it. So far the 2 who put the log outside their two chose the schedule and subs not showing, so test whether chasing subs is the bigger pain. Also say why Current solution has no line here.

screens.why1: First thing they'd need to know is whether my jobs actually run on Procore or ACC, so it makes sense as the opening screener.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms every super I know works in daily, and 'a job you run' is how we talk about it.
screens.why3: I know exactly which platform my current job is on; the GC set it up and I log in every day.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it, and a job on both or one of each is still a clean yes.
screens.why5: It just checks the platform I'm on, and nothing about the founder's product or plan comes through.
screens.why6: Short and easy to answer by ear, but 'I'll read 2 options' is clunky for a yes-or-no, and the guidelines say a screener is spoken as the stem then 'Yes or no.'
screens.instead: Is any job you run now on Procore or ACC? Yes or no.

screens.why1: After asking if I run a job on Procore or ACC, asking whether I did a daily log this week is the obvious next gate before asking about my last one.
screens.why2: It is two questions in one: did I do a log, and did it take hours. Some days the log takes me 40 minutes and some days most of the evening, so I'm not sure whether to say yes or no.
screens.why3: I put together a daily log every working day, photos and notes into Procore, so I can answer this straight from my week.
screens.why4: Yes and No are fine, but a gate should have no escape, and here there are two; 'I'd rather not say' isn't allowed, and 'I can't recall one particular daily log' makes no sense for a yes-or-no about the whole week.
screens.why5: 'Spend hours typing up' puts the founder's pain into the screener; whether it takes hours is what the study should find out, not a condition for getting in, and much of my time goes on uploading photos, not typing.
screens.why6: Heard once it is short and ends in 'Yes or no', and the spoken form rightly drops the chips, though the word 'hours' still makes me stop and think.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you put together a daily log for one of your jobs? Yes or no.

screens.why1: I just said yes to spending hours on the log this week, so asking how many of the five days that happened is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Daily log, typing it up, last five working days: that's my language and I can answer it on first read.
screens.why3: I know which nights this week I sat in the trailer late getting the log into Procore, so I can count them.
screens.why4: One through five covers it after a yes, the numbers don't overlap, and I can't recall fits if the week was a blur.
screens.why5: Most of my time goes to getting the photos and notes in, not typing, so 'typing up' narrows what actually eats the hours.
screens.why6: One short question and 'a number from 1 to 5' is easy to hold, so I can answer straight off when I hear it.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, on how many days did getting your photos and notes into the daily log take you hours? 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · 5 · I can't recall

screens.why1: After two questions about the daily log, asking which part of my week I'd most want easier is the natural next step to see if the log really matters to me.
screens.why2: RFIs, submittals, subs, the daily log: those are the words on my site every day, and I can answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: These five are exactly what eats a superintendent's week, so I can pick from what I actually did last week.
screens.why4: Keeping the job on schedule and getting subs to show up and finish overlap, since subs not showing is most of why a schedule slips; None of these fits as the escape.
screens.why5: Nothing about a product, an AI or a scribe reaches me; it's just my own work listed in my words.
screens.why6: One short question, five short options I can hold, and RFIs is said in the trailer every day so it carries fine spoken.
screens.instead: Think of your last week on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Chasing RFIs and submittals; Keeping the three-week lookahead on track; Writing up the daily log; Keeping the site safe; Getting subs to show up and finish. Or say none of these.

screens.why1: Asking how my last log went fits after the hours questions, but 'took a couple of hours' goes back over what screens 2 and 3 already got out of me.
screens.why2: The question asks how the photo upload went, but the answers are about where and when the whole log got finished, so I'd have to read it twice to work out which one I'm answering.
screens.why3: I did a daily log last week and I know exactly how the photos got into Procore and when I finished.
screens.why4: The five are distinct and in my words, but they don't answer the photo question; there's no 'uploaded from my phone as I walked' or 'Procore was slow and I sat waiting on it', and 'Log done on site' says nothing about the photos.
screens.why5: It keeps to the photos, the daily log and the hours after the walk, and nothing about anybody's product reaches me.
screens.why6: Short stem, five short options I can hold, one escape at the end, and it says easily.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. When did you finish getting the site photos into it? Done from my phone during the walk; done in the trailer in under an hour; took a couple of hours after the walk; finished at home or the next morning; never got them all in. Or say you can't recall.
